candidates.differences: Genesis describes Adam assigning names to animals brought before him; Qur'an describes God teaching Adam all the names and testing angels, without limiting names to animals.

rows.theme: Adam and spouse inhabit garden, forbidden tree

candidates.shared: A first human pair in a garden faces a prohibition concerning a tree.
candidates.differences: Genesis names a tree of knowledge of good and evil, narrates the serpent speaking to the woman and eating; Qur'an 2:35 does not identify the tree, and the warning names Satan as an enemy in nearby context.

rows.theme: Satan causes fall; descent and mutual enmity

candidates.shared: Transgression of a divine garden prohibition precedes departure from the garden.
candidates.differences: Genesis attributes the temptation to the serpent, describes judgments on serpent, woman and man and expulsion; Qur'an 2:36 attributes the slip to Satan, speaks of descent and enmity and a temporary earthly abode.

rows.notes: No claim of exhaustive screening or historical dependence; source-critical verification pending.

rows.theme: Adam receives words and divine turning in mercy

candidates.shared: Both narratives continue after the garden violation.
candidates.differences: Qur'an explicitly reports Adam receiving words and God turning toward him in mercy; Genesis 3:21–24 describes garments, exclusion and cherubim without the corresponding explicit repentance formula.

rows.notes: No claim of exhaustive screening or historical dependence; source-critical verification pending.

rows.theme: Descent and future guidance; response to guidance

candidates.shared: Both passages concern human life after departure from the garden.
candidates.differences: Qur'an promises future divine guidance and freedom from fear/grief for followers; Genesis describes exclusion from the tree of life and guarding the garden, not this guidance formula.
